s:
With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements :
I. The Governor of a State is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office.
II. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted or continued against the Governor during his/her term of office.
III. Members of a State Legislature are not liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said within the House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Article 361 of the Constitution of India grants special protection from legal accountability to the President and the Governor. Under Article 361(1), the Governor is not answerable to any court for acts done in the exercise of the powers and duties of his office. The same Article 361 under clause (2) clearly states that, during the Governor’s term of office (same in the case of the President), no criminal proceedings of any kind can be instituted, nor can such proceedings be continued. In this manner, he enjoys complete criminal immunity during his tenure. The provision regarding privileges and immunity for members of the State Legislature is contained in Article 194(2) of the Constitution. According to it, no member of a State Legislature shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by him in the Legislature or any committee thereof. This immunity is absolute, provided the proceedings relate to something said or a vote given within the House or any of its committees. Thus, all three statements are in accordance with the constitutional provisions; therefore, the correct answer is option (d).
